notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #12
notes.content:
Ahoy!

In today’s devlog, we want to show you a bit of the world we’ve designed for the game—one that you’ll be able to explore with your crew and your ship. Keep in mind, though, that the places you visit might hide valuable treasures, but they also come with dangers. Sometimes, you’ll run into trouble, like the Trade Company trying to stop you.

In this post, we’ll give you a closer look at a few interesting locations you can visit on the map—and what you might expect to find there.

[h3]The Quiet Shores – Fishing Village[/h3]

[i]"Aye, the fish be fresh an’ the winds be calm... but don’t expect more than a dry biscuit and a silent stare." — Old Red Flit, sailor and lover of quiet ports[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/253db89a28f61dcbb902bca2c3befc3d8cc86cee.jpg[/img]

One of the locations you can visit is a peaceful fishing village. This small settlement offers basic supplies—most importantly, food, which becomes crucial for aiding the nearby burned city.

Nothing out of the ordinary happens here. It’s a quiet, safe place, perfect for resting and preparing for the journey ahead.

[h3]Ashes of Seashell Bay – Burned Harbor[/h3]

[i]"Used to be a fine port, it was... now is’s just smoke, screams, and beggin’ eyes. Best bring more than pity, mate." — First Mate Grigory, witness to the burning[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/fd46cd005533346a578ef4e3db4f1b795ad26735.jpg[/img]

Seashell Bay Harbor is a ruined city, recently devastated by an attack from the Trade Company. Its people are struggling to survive and have little to offer, except a desperate need for resources and support.

[h3]The Storm’s Refuge – Atoll Fort[/h3]

[i]"Ye don’t stroll into that atoll, lad – not unless ye fancy dancin’ cannonballs with Captain Storm hisself!" — Captain Rakes, survivor of the Outer Fort Clash[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/98cd51cf19a4d4b98ffbb9f4370204f43d55cfba.jpg[/img]

At the heart of a remote atoll lies a small settlement guarded by a powerful fort. It’s a Trade Company-controlled area located on the edge of their territory and home to the infamous Captain Otto, also known as “The Storm.”

Reaching this place is no easy task — you must first deal with the fort. A key moment involves ambushing a supply convoy to weaken its defenses. 

[h3]The Totem Watchers – Seeker Research Camp[/h3]

[i]"They say they study totems... but I swear by me compass, those Seeker rats got darker plans than they let on." — Black-eye Jack, ex-cultist turned smuggler[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/04f3da5c19883ec996e9b7b647de3ea7f9cf7d32.jpg[/img]

On one of the islands, a camp of strangers studying a mysterious totem linked to the local tribes can be found. These outsiders call themselves the “Seekers of Order” and seem to be engaged in odd rituals and research.

[h3]Black Rocks Haven – Pirate Hideout[/h3]

[i]"Now this be a place fer real sailors—no law, no questions, just rum, powder, an’ coin changin’ hands." — Joe, quartermaster and fence[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/149a338bc9d48ed296f35e42443cb06d6f4c694d.jpg[/img]

Hidden among sharp coastal rocks is a small pirate hideout. It's one of the few places where players can resupply deep within Trade Company territory.

This hideout serves as a launch point for raids against fishing villages and enemy camps. It’s also a black market hub where looted goods — especially from Seeker camps — can be sold. Despite its location in hostile lands, the hideout itself remains safe and free from immediate threats.

[h3]Flames of Disorder – Burning Seeker Camp[/h3]

[i]"I’ve sailed through ghost waters an’ stared down storms, but I swear on Blackbeard’s beard—I ain’t stayin’ the night in that camp." — Old Man Hank, last seen leavin’ without his boots[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/e37300a3323cd7c2a696730ac3c3fae8e2fda85f.jpg[/img]

Hidden on the edge of archipelago island, Whispershade Hollow is a quiet, unsettling encampment. The people here are... strange. They speak in riddles, move in silence, and seem to worship something they never name aloud. Whether they’re mystics, fanatics, or madmen is anyone’s guess — but none of them seem entirely sane.

There are whispers of secret rituals, strange symbols carved into trees, and a presence in the air that chills even the boldest pirate to the bone. 

[h3]Deadman’s Nook – Pirate Hideout in Company Lands[/h3]

[i]"Only a madman or a true pirate sets up shop this deep in Company waters... lucky fer us, I be both."  — Scarface Jim, founder of the Nook[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/47371e5da302ac4e592a14029ebd6f826f03f673.jpg[/img]

Deadman’s Nook is a hidden pirate outpost tucked right into the heart of Trade Company territory. It’s a rough, quiet place, carved out of desperation and defiance. The pirates here keep their heads low and blades ready—every supply run could be the last.

Despite the risk, it’s one of the few places where players can resupply behind enemy lines. Black market deals, whispered plans, and forbidden maps often pass through this little outpost—if you know who to talk to.

[h3]Shark Bay Harbor – Trade Company controlled Port[/h3]

[i]"They call it order. I call it chains in velvet gloves." — Mistress Vyra, pirate with unfinished business[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f673efa348ddd40be1ae26694d9ccde6ccc41222.jpg[/img]

Shark Bay Harbor is a bustling Trade Company port, strictly controlled and heavily patrolled. Outsiders are met with suspicion, and pirates even more so. The city is a fortress of “law” and profit for the Trading Company itself — but the cracks are starting to show.

While it begins as a hostile zone, some choices and actions may slowly turn the tides. Influence can be gained. Loyalties can be shaken. Perhaps even this Company stronghold can be turned to your advantage… for a price.

[h3]Ironhold Bastion – Fortress of Samuel “Iron Hand”[/h3]

[i]"I once tried to sail past Ironhold at night... the stars vanished from the cannon smoke. I ain’t goin’ back." — Blind Pete, survivor of the Night Barrage[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f2b53c0e2b9ce0b07874e15b6cc9dc6d6fe5ed00.jpg[/img]

Ironhold Bastion is the crown jewel of the Trade Company’s military might—a fortified island citadel, guarded by cannons, sea mines, and the flagship frigate of the infamous Samuel "Iron Hand", the Company’s ruthless leader.

Approaching this place without a plan is madness. The bastion is not just a stronghold—it’s a symbol. Taking it means striking at the very heart of the Company’s power. It won’t be easy, and it won’t be quiet… but it might just be legendary.

That’s all we’ve prepared for you today. We hope you enjoyed it, and we’d love to hear what you think in the comments below!

Remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!

notes.title: Pirate Commander - Registration for playtests is now open!
notes.content:
[h3]Greetings, adventurers! We're thrilled to announce an exclusive opportunity for you to dive into the turbulent waters of Pirate Commander, before it officially sets sail. This is your chance to lead a life of daring piracy, navigate through uncharted waters, and leave your mark on this thrilling world.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/597a826e506f9d4e4aa4ca0ef93596e70bd1bcd2.png[/img]

[h3]Why Join Our Playtests?[/h3]

This is not just an invitation to play a game; it's a call to shape its future. By joining our playtests, you'll have the opportunity to:

[list]


[*] Experience Pirate Commander firsthand: Get an exclusive sneak peek into the game's mechanics, graphics, and unique features before its official release.

[*] Provide valuable feedback: Your insights are crucial. Help us refine gameplay, balance, and user experience by sharing your thoughts and suggestions.

[*] Influence the final product: Your feedback can lead to real changes in the game, ensuring a better experience for all players upon release.

[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/cdc4706db1ced8ff241d26de29ccc1b87cd1e8c2.png[/img]


Ready to hoist the sails and join this thrilling adventure? Joining our playtests is simple:


[list]
[*] Navigate to the Pirate Commander Steam page.

[*] Look for the "Request to Playtest" button and click on it.

[*] Follow the instructions to sign up for the playtest.
[/list]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1359270/Pirate_Commander/


Spots are limited, so make sure to sign up quickly to secure your place in this adventure. Whether you're a seasoned sailor of digital seas or a newcomer eager to embark on your first voyage, Pirate Commander promises a journey filled with excitement, strategy, and peril.

notes.title: Pirate Commander - DevLog #4
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f93205bfbba7063b51815c830069850b909ca99a.jpg[/img]
Hello sailors!

The captain and his crew must travel through many distant lands on their way to wealth and glory. To survive the dangers lurking there, you will first need to prepare both the ship and the crew. To do this, you need to collect the necessary resources and properly build the ship, ensuring that you have enough gold for your crew pay and enough supply of cheering potion for sea wolves - rum.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/4ec8bc26fb93e29ad62a143bb516fb1b111b694a.jpg[/img]
There are several resources that you can gather in Pirate Commander during the exploration of the Archipelago. Some examples of them are as follows:
1. wood - the basic building material for both the ship and the cabins

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/f2a59bd7b2e31b9ea8caa7d4c3488eef65a170f8.jpg[/img]
2. metal - is an essential raw material for creating metal elements of the ship, including cabins and weapons as well as tools to repair the ship

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/d3f317aa362fdfdb1fc0c1a57b6a546050fd0fe9.jpg[/img]
3. herbs - a raw material used by alchemists to brew healing potions necessary for each sea wolf to heal after the combat

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/308fa4a1f774243785c149116bdb23176e055315.jpg[/img]
4. gold - a resource obtained by completing tasks, robberies, selling goods, etc. Gold is a universal currency opening every path, so it allows you to buy other resources, pay your crew, and more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/9b4af640f69d606c18a85770729ccdb027150561.jpg[/img]
In order to find introduced resources there are several ways to do so. 

The first one is the exploration of the map in the search of raw material stockpiles. Unfortunately, this method of increasing the number of resources is not the best one. Although it offers a free and easy way to fill in your warehouses, it is just a one-time use only. Once the resource stockpile is collected, it is no longer available.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/1d7e8f209d1890b3235abeca7f42d0de19b02387.jpg[/img]
The second way to obtain resources (more reliable) is to find the merchants scattered over the archipelago. Merchants are able to sell you the produced raw material for a certain amount of gold. It is worth noting that they only have a limited amount of resources to sell at once, but they are replenished from time to time. It is, therefore, worth planning your trip first to visit several of them during a single voyage from one port to another.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/a8179a2f6e79a1519fe737284281b692052ab678.jpg[/img]

There will be more options for you to collect needed resources like performing quests, visiting distant ports, and of course, plundering other ships but we will talk about them more in future Dev Logs. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38779553/0297801fdefcdecd75f1ffe2b356c9da2983b434.jpg[/img]
Stay tuned for more news from Pirate Commander development in the upcoming weeks. 

Fair winds and following seas! 



Also remember to follow us on social media and join our discord server!
